_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-21 06:33:04Z)**_

確認結論：

| 項目 | 值 |
|---|---|
| PATH 上的 rsync | 只有 `/usr/bin/rsync`（系統內建） |
| 實際實作 | **openrsync**，`rsync 2.6.9 compatible`、protocol 29 |
| Homebrew rsync | **未安裝**（`/opt/homebrew/bin`、`/usr/local/bin` 都沒有） |

所以你的診斷完全正確：失敗不是因為 GNU rsync 太舊，而是 macOS 現在根本沒裝 GNU rsync——`/usr/bin/rsync` 是 Apple 的 openrsync，只兼容到 2.6.9 語意，`--info`（GNU rsync 3.1+ 才有）直接不認。

**修法**：裝 Homebrew 版的 GNU rsync（3.x），它會落在 `/opt/homebrew/bin/rsync`，因為 brew path 排在 `/usr/bin` 前面，`rsync` 就會自動指向新版：

```bash
brew install rsync
```

裝完驗證：

```bash
rsync --version   # 應該看到 "rsync  version 3.4.x  protocol version 32"
```

49	## Install order
50	
51	Five phases in chronological order. Anything earlier MUST be present
52	before the next phase can run.
53	
54	```
55	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
56	│ Phase 0 — Bootstrap (run_once_before_*)                                 │
57	│   curl-installer: Homebrew, uv, mise                                    │
58	│   apt: build-essential, git, curl (Linux prereqs for Linuxbrew)         │
59	│   apt: libffi-dev, libyaml-dev, python3-dev (Linux non-noRoot only)     │
60	│   uv: ansible-core (pinned Python 3.13)                                 │
61	│   ansible-galaxy: community.general collection                          │
62	│   mise: install runtimes from ~/.config/mise/config.toml                │
63	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
64	                                  │
65	                                  ▼
66	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
67	│ Phase 1 — chezmoi apply (config file deploy)                            │
68	│   Deploys dot_* files; doesn't install tools directly                   │
69	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
70	                                  │
71	                                  ▼
72	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
73	│ Phase 2 — Ansible (run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles)                 │
74	│   Runs all 26 roles; each dispatches to its underlying manager          │
75	│   (brew / apt / mise / uv / npm / cargo / gem / dotnet / curl / gh-rel) │
76	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
77	                                  │
78	                                  ▼
79	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
80	│ Phase 3 — Brew bundle (run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle)               │
81	│   `brew bundle --no-upgrade` against ~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile*       │
82	│   Mostly GUI casks (macOS); skipped unless Brew/AI/gaming apps enabled  │
83	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
84	                                  │
85	                                  ▼
86	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
87	│ Phase 4 — Per-application onchange scripts                              │
88	│   Completion regen (run_after_50_generate_completions)                  │
89	│   bat theme cache (run_onchange_after_25_bat_theme)                     │
90	│   ble.sh compile (run_onchange_after_26_install_blesh)                  │
91	│   Global skills restore (run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills)   │
92	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
93	```
94	
95	The bootstrap is **single-source-of-truth** for the foundational tools
96	that everything else depends on. If you find yourself wanting to add
97	`mise` / `uv` / Homebrew elsewhere, the answer is almost always "extend
98	the bootstrap, then assume it in the role". The Linux noRoot path
99	(`profile=ubuntu_server` or RHEL/CentOS without sudo) skips the apt
100	prereqs and Linuxbrew, falling back to per-tool curl-installers and
101	GitHub releases — coverage is intentionally narrower (no GUI, no
102	system-wide installs).
103

106	## Per-manager catalog
107	
108	Each subsection below covers one manager. Format:
109	
110	- **Owns** — what tools end up under this manager's control
111	- **How a tool gets there** — the canonical "I want to add tool X via this manager" recipe
112	- **Per-OS notes** — branching when relevant
113	- **Upgrade path** — link to the matching category in `upgrades.md`
114	
115	The ansible roles section is split into thematic subsections because
116	26 roles in one table is unreadable.
117	
118	### 1. Bootstrap scripts (pre-chezmoi)
119	
120	**Files**: `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl`,
121	`run_once_before_02_fix_intel_homebrew.sh.tmpl`,
122	`run_once_before_50_opencode_migrate.sh.tmpl`
123	
124	**Owns** — the four foundational managers that everything else
125	assumes:
126	
127	| Tool | Mechanism | Per-OS |
128	|---|---|---|
129	| **Homebrew** | `Homebrew/install` curl script | macOS always; Linux only when `installBrewApps=true` & non-noRoot & arch∈{amd64,arm64}. Mirrors via `HOMEBREW_BREW_GIT_REMOTE` + bottle/API domains (**BFSU** baseline; `brew-mirror` switches to USTC/Aliyun/TUNA) when `useChineseMirror=true`. Aliyun's `brew.git` is broken (hangs) and `HOMEBREW_CORE_GIT_REMOTE` stays unset (API mode) — see [mirrors.md](../tools/mirrors.md#brew-update--any-brew-command-hangs-for-60s-then-does-nothing) |
130	| **uv** | `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh \| sh` | all OSes if missing |
131	| **mise** | `curl https://mise.run \| sh`, with direct `mise.jdx.dev/mise-latest-linux-${arch}[-musl]` fallback (musl forced when glibc < 2.28) | all OSes; arch detection (x64/arm64/armv7) |
132	| **ansible-core** | `uv tool install --force --python 3.13 ansible-core` | all OSes; force-refreshes if existing ansible runs on Python < 3.10 |
133	| **ansible-galaxy: community.general** | `ansible-galaxy collection install --force-with-deps` | all OSes |
134	| **mise runtimes** | `mise install --yes` (consumes `~/.config/mise/config.toml`) | all OSes — see [§ mise](#4-mise-runtime-versions) |
135	
136	**Linux prereqs (apt)** to make Linuxbrew + mise Ruby + ansible-cryptography
137	buildable: `build-essential`, `procps`, `curl`, `file`, `git` (always);
138	`libffi-dev`, `libyaml-dev`, `python3-dev` (non-noRoot only).
139	
140	**Intel-Mac-only side script**: `run_once_before_02_fix_intel_homebrew.sh.tmpl`
141	runs `softwareupdate -i` for Xcode CLT, then `brew cleanup` +
142	`brew link --overwrite git`.
143	
144	**One-shot migrations**: `run_once_before_50_opencode_migrate.sh.tmpl`
145	moves a legacy config file (`~/.config/opencode/config.json` →
146	`opencode.json`). Not an install.
147	
148	**Adding to bootstrap**: only when the new tool is required *before*
149	ansible runs — e.g. ansible itself, mise (because ansible roles call
150	`mise exec`), uv (because some roles call `uv tool install`). Otherwise
151	prefer an ansible role.

153	### 2. Homebrew (formulae + casks)
154	
155	Three Brewfile templates + scattered `community.general.homebrew[_cask]`
156	tasks in ansible roles. The split is **macOS-centric**: Linux Brewfile is
157	empty, Linuxbrew use happens role-by-role.
158	
159	#### 2.1 Brewfiles
160	
161	| File | Owns |
162	|---|---|

189	#### 2.2 Role-driven brew (formulae + casks)
190	
191	Most CLI formulae land via ansible roles, not the Brewfile. Examples:
192	
193	- `base/tasks/main.yml`: `git`, `git-lfs`, `curl`, `wget`, `ripgrep`, `fd`, `jq`, `tree`, `just`
194	- `devtools/tasks/main.yml`: large set — `bat`, `gh`, `glab`, `diffnav`, `git-delta`, `eza`, `tlrc`, `glow`, `gum`, `vhs`, `freeze`, `thefuck`, `zoxide`, `direnv`, `yazi`, `superfile`, `tmux`, `sesh`, `worktrunk`, `workmux`, `zellij`, `btop`, `htop`, `duckdb`, `rclone`, `coreutils`, `taplo`, `television`, `pandoc`, `tailspin`, `lnav`, `grc`, `dasel`, `yq`, `jnv`, `witr`, `figlet`, `toilet`, `lolcat`, `fastfetch`, `shellcheck`, `shfmt`, `bats-core`, `git-graph`, `mosh`, `doxx`, `libreoffice`
195	- `coding_agents/tasks/main.yml`: `claude-code` (cask), `codex` (cask), `gemini-cli` (formula), `rtk` (formula), `specstory`, `codexbar`, `td`, `sidecar` (all with tap setup)
196	- `networking_tools/`: `nmap`, `arp-scan`, `mtr`, `iperf3`, `doggo`, `httpie`, `gping`, `trippy`, `bandwhich`, `rustscan`, `speedtest` (tap `teamookla/speedtest`), `ngrok`, `cloudflared`
197	- `media_tools/`: `ffmpeg`, `imagemagick`, `exiftool`, `vips`
198	- `iac_tools/`: `azure-cli`, `hashicorp/tap/terraform`, `opentofu`
199	- `llm_tools/`: `llmfit`, `models`, `ollama`
200	- `security_tools/`: `gitleaks`
201	- `starship/`, `atuin/`, `neovim/`, `bash/` (gawk), `zsh/` — each installs its primary tool via homebrew formula on macOS
202	- `pueue` (from `rust_cargo_tools/`): macOS uses homebrew formula
203	
204	**Per-OS dispatch** is the universal pattern in roles: macOS branch uses
205	`community.general.homebrew` / `homebrew_cask`; Linux branches use apt,
206	Linuxbrew (when present), or GitHub releases. See each role for the
207	explicit `when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"` guard.
208	
209	**Tap inventory** (added by various roles): `nikitabobko/tap`,
210	`wxtsky/tap` (CodeIsland), `hashicorp/tap` (terraform),
211	`teamookla/speedtest`, `specstoryai/tap`, `steipete/tap` (CodexBar),
212	`marcus/tap` (td, sidecar), `dlvhdr/formulae`, `raine/workmux`.
213	
214	Homebrew 6+ refuses formulae/casks from untrusted third-party taps. Role-driven
215	taps must run a `brew tap-info <tap>` → `brew trust <tap>` check before installing
216	from that tap; Brewfile taps are handled by the brew-bundle run-script before it
217	calls `brew bundle`. See
218	[`pitfalls/homebrew-6-refuses-untrusted-tap-formula.md`](../../pitfalls/homebrew-6-refuses-untrusted-tap-formula.md).
219	
220	**Adding via homebrew**: prefer a brew formula/cask only when the tool
221	is macOS-shipped and Linux equivalents go via apt or release tarball.
222	Linux-first tools rarely belong in the Brewfile.
223	
224	#### 2.3 Homebrew prefix dispatch helper
225	
226	`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::_uv_install_style` (and mirrored helpers in
227	`python_uv_tools/tasks/main.yml`) inspect whether a binary lives under
228	`brew --prefix` to decide between `brew upgrade <pkg>` and the tool's
229	native self-update. This avoids the "I `uv self update` on a brew-uv
230	host and silently no-op" trap — see
231	[`pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md).
232	
233	### 3. Ansible roles
234	
235	26 roles under `dot_ansible/roles/`. Triggered by
236	`.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`
237	(re-runs when any role's `tasks/main.yml` or `defaults/main.yml` changes
238	— SHA256-tracked).
239	
240	**Universal patterns**:
241	
242	- `state: present` / `creates:` — install-only, no silent upgrades
243	- Per-OS branching via `when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"` (or `["Debian", "RedHat"]`)
244	- `tags: [sudo]` on any `become: true` task (so noRoot mode skips them — see [`pitfalls/ansible-missing-sudo-tag.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/ansible-missing-sudo-tag.md))
245	- `failed_when: false` + `register:` for "is the tool installed?" probes
246	- Linux user-level fallback to `~/.local/bin` when distro package is missing or too old (handles RHEL/CentOS + noRoot + Apple-Silicon-not-bottled scenarios)
247	
248	**Role feature flags** (set in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` via prompts):
249	`installBrewApps`, `installAiDesktopApps`, `installCodingAgents`,
250	`installLlmTools`, `installPythonUvTools`, `installJsCliTools`,
251	`installDotnetTools`, `installIacTools`, `installMediaTools`,
252	`installNetworkingTools`, `installTunnelTools`, `installBitwarden`,
253	`installGamingApps`, `installInputMethod`, `installAuditd`. Roles gate themselves on the
254	matching flag; the bundle script `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` defines
255	profile presets (`minimal`, `cloud-vm` planned, default-developer, …).
256	
257	#### 3.1 Base / shared CLI
258	
259	| Role | Owns | Per-OS mechanism |
260	|---|---|---|
261	| `base` | `git`, `git-lfs`, `curl`, `wget`, `ripgrep`, `fd`, `jq`, `tree`, `just`, `gcc`/`build-essential`/`make` | macOS: brew formulae · Debian: apt (`fd-find` + `/usr/bin/fd` symlink) · RedHat: yum · `just` always via `curl https://just.systems/install.sh` · Linux user-level GitHub-release fallback to `~/.local/bin` for ripgrep/fd/jq/git-lfs |
262	| `homebrew` | (no installs — refresh + cleanup only, 24h-throttled) | n/a |
263	| `atuin` | `atuin` shell history sync | macOS: brew formula · Linux: `curl https://setup.atuin.sh \| sh -s -- --non-interactive` → `~/.atuin/bin/` |
264	| `nerdfonts` | `font-hack-nerd-font` | macOS: brew cask · Linux: download `Hack.zip` from `nerd-fonts/releases/latest` → `~/.local/share/fonts` + `fc-cache -fv` |
265	
266	#### 3.2 Shells (`bash`, `zsh`, `starship`)
267	
268	| Role | Owns | Per-OS mechanism |
269	|---|---|---|
270	| `bash` | `gawk` (ble.sh dep, unconditional); homebrew `bash` 5.x + `/etc/shells` + `chsh` (macOS only when `primary_shell="bash"`) | macOS: brew · Debian: apt · RedHat: yum |
271	| `zsh` | system `zsh` package; **source-build zsh 5.9** to `~/.local` on RHEL/CentOS 7 if system zsh < 5.3; `chsh` when `primary_shell="zsh"` (default) | macOS: brew · Debian: apt · RedHat: yum + ncurses-devel source build fallback. oh-my-zsh + plugins ship as externals (§12) |
272	| `starship` | `starship` prompt | macOS: brew formula · Linux: `curl https://starship.rs/install.sh \| sh -s -- --yes` → sudo `/usr/local/bin` → user `~/.local/bin` fallback |
273	
274	The `primaryShell` chezmoi prompt gates the `chsh` call only — both
275	shells deploy their configs everywhere. See AGENTS.md → "`primaryShell`
276	choice gates `chsh` only" hard invariant.

See [`pitfalls/opencode-docker-opentui-glibc-loader-missing.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/opencode-docker-opentui-glibc-loader-missing.md) for the container-image variant |

405	### 4. mise (runtime versions)
406	
407	**Config**: `dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl`
408	
409	`[settings]`: `ruby.compile = false`.

411	**Modern hosts** (default):
412	
413	| Runtime | Version | Gated on |
414	|---|---|---|
415	| `node` | `lts` | always |
416	| `bun` | `1` | `installExtraRuntimes` |
417	| `rust` | `stable` | `installExtraRuntimes` |
418	| `go` | `latest` | `installExtraRuntimes` |
419	| `dotnet` | `10` | `installDotnetTools` |
420	| `ruby` | `3` | `installExtraRuntimes` (+ not `noRoot`) |
421	
422	**Version-pinning rationale**: `node=lts` / `rust=stable` / `go=latest` use
423	moving channels because each promises backward compatibility (Go's
424	[go1compat](https://go.dev/doc/go1compat) makes `latest` as safe as
425	rust's `stable`). `bun=1` and `dotnet=10` pin the **major** instead —
426	neither guarantees no-break across majors (bun ships behavior changes on
427	minors; .NET majors bump TFMs / SDK behavior), and `dotnet=10` is also the
428	current LTS (8/9 are at/near EOL by mid-2026). Bump `dotnet` deliberately
429	when the next LTS (12) lands. `ruby=3` tracks the 3.x line.
430	
431	`go` replaces the old macOS-only brew install from the `security_tools`
432	role, so Linux hosts now get a managed Go too (previously a gap).
433	
434	Ruby is **skipped in noRoot mode** (`profile=ubuntu_server` without
435	sudo) because it needs `libffi-dev` / `libyaml-dev` to build, which
436	require apt.
437	
438	**oldEL (CentOS/RHEL 7, glibc 2.17)**: only `ruby = "3"` — other
439	runtimes have glibc/libstdc++ requirements too new for EL7.
440	
441	**Upgrade**: `just upgrade-mise` → `mise self-update --yes` + `mise upgrade`
442	(honours the version constraints in the config; `lts`/`latest` move
443	forward, pinned versions don't).
444	
445	**Adding a runtime**: edit `dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl` directly.
446	Runtime-version gating across hosts is on the [backlog](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/mise-runtime-gating.md).
447	
448	**Why mise (not nvm/rbenv/pyenv/asdf/n)**: unified, language-agnostic,
449	respects `.tool-versions`, doesn't fight shell init order. Python is
450	deliberately **not** mise-managed — that's uv's territory (faster + no
451	build-from-source for CPython, which the noRoot Linux path can't do).
452	The [backlog](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/mise-runtime-gating.md) tracks
453	finer-grained per-host gating.
454

510	### 6. npm (global Node CLIs)
511	
512	**Config**: `dot_ansible/roles/js_cli_tools/defaults/main.yml` for the
513	JS-tools-specific list. Scattered global-npm installs live in other
514	roles (`coding_agents`, `bitwarden`, `lazyvim_deps`, `devtools`).
515	
516	**Install dispatch** (universal pattern across roles):
517	
518	```yaml
519	# On Linux:
520	mise exec -- npm install -g <package>
521	# Falls back to system npm if mise has no node registered
522	# On macOS:
523	community.general.npm: { name: <package>, global: true }
524	```
525	
526	Linux explicitly uses `mise exec -- npm` to avoid the Ubuntu apt npm
527	(too old; system Node 12 fails `engine` checks for modern packages and
528	`/usr/local/lib/node_modules` is root-owned, breaking `--global` for
529	non-root users). See [`pitfalls/ansible-js-cli-tools-old-system-node.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/ansible-js-cli-tools-old-system-node.md).
530	
531	**Inventory**:
532	
533	| Package | Binary | Role / line |
534	|---|---|---|
535	| `readability-cli` | `readable` | `js_cli_tools/defaults/main.yml` |
536	| `@bitwarden/cli` | `bw` | `bitwarden/tasks/main.yml` |
537	| `@githubnext/github-copilot-cli` | `github-copilot-cli` | `coding_agents/tasks/main.yml:134-168` |
538	| `@openai/codex` | `codex` (Linux only — macOS uses brew cask) | `coding_agents/tasks/main.yml:172-236` |
539	| `@google/gemini-cli` | `gemini` (Linux always; macOS fallback if brew formula fails) | `coding_agents/tasks/main.yml:240-300` |
540	| `@openchamber/web` | `openchamber` | `coding_agents/tasks/main.yml:1188-1222` |
541	| `tldr` | `tldr` (Linux only — macOS uses `tlrc` via brew) | `devtools/tasks/main.yml` |
542	| `tree-sitter-cli` | `tree-sitter` | `lazyvim_deps/tasks/main.yml` (preferred over cargo fallback) |
543	
544	**Upgrade**: `just upgrade-npm` → `npm -g update` with `mise exec --`
545	fallback.
546	
547	**Adding an npm tool**: append to `js_cli_tools/defaults/main.yml` (for
548	general utilities); for an agent CLI, add the install task to
549	`coding_agents/tasks/main.yml` matching the existing dispatch pattern
550	(macOS via system npm, Linux via `mise exec -- npm install -g`).

553	
554	**Config**: `dot_ansible/roles/rust_cargo_tools/defaults/main.yml`
555	(currently `cargo_tools: []` — no generic entries).
556	
557	**Rust install**: `mise install rust@latest` (preferred), with two
558	fallback layers on noRoot/oldEL boxes: direct `rustup-init`, then
559	`https://static.rust-lang.org` when the configured mirror's manifest
560	is stale.
561	
562	**Inventory** (hard-coded in `tasks/main.yml`):
563	
564	| Crate | Mechanism | Notes |
565	|---|---|---|
566	| `recon` | `cargo install --git https://github.com/gavraz/recon --locked` | git source (no crates.io publish yet) |
567	| `pueue` | macOS brew formula; Linux `cargo install pueue --locked` | + `pueued.service` systemd user unit; version check `pueue_min_version=4.0.0` (warn-only) |
568	| `tree-sitter-cli` | `cargo install tree-sitter-cli` (fallback only) | preferred path is `mise exec -- npm install -g tree-sitter-cli`; cargo path installs `libclang-dev`/`clang-devel` first |
569	| `alacritty` | cargo build (`gui_apps_linux`) | requires apt build deps (`cmake`, `pkg-config`, `libfontconfig1-dev`, `libxcb-xfixes0-dev`, `libxkbcommon-dev`) |
570	| `modelsdev` | cargo fallback (`llm_tools`) | only when Linuxbrew not present + brew formula `models` not available |
571	| `cargo-update` | `cargo install cargo-update` (bootstrap for upgrade) | installed by `upgrade_tools.sh::cat_cargo` on first run, then `cargo install-update -a` uses it |
572	
573	**Upgrade**: `just upgrade-cargo` → `cargo install-update -a` (which
574	covers everything installed via cargo, including pueue on Linux).
575	
576	**Adding a cargo tool**: prefer `cargo_tools: [<name>]` in the defaults
577	YAML (covered by `cargo install-update -a`); hard-code in `tasks/main.yml`
578	only when the install needs extra build deps or a non-crates.io source
579	(see `recon`, `pueue`).

581	### 8. go (Go CLI tools)
582	
583	**Config**: `dot_ansible/roles/go_tools/defaults/main.yml`
584	
585	**Go install**: the Go toolchain ships via mise (`go = "latest"`, gated on
586	`installExtraRuntimes`). The role resolves the mise Go bin dir via
587	`mise which go` and no-ops cleanly when Go is absent (so lean/CI hosts skip
588	it). Binaries install into `~/.local/bin` via `GOBIN` (already on PATH via
589	`dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl`) — not `~/go/bin` (`GOPATH/bin`) or the
590	version-pinned mise toolchain dir. A `creates:` guard makes the install
591	idempotent.
592	
593	**Inventory**:
594	
595	| Package | Binary |
596	|---|---|
597	| `github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@v0.1.0` | `translate` (Linux only; macOS → Homebrew `daviddwlee84/tap/translate`) |
598	
599	**Upgrade**: `just upgrade-go` → `go install <pkg>@latest` per entry (strips
600	the pinned version). Install pins a known-good version for reproducible fresh
601	boxes; upgrades move it forward — the same install-vs-upgrade split as cargo.
602	
603	**Adding a go tool**: append to `go_tools/defaults/main.yml` with `name`
604	(`<module-path>@<version>`) and `binary` (the resulting command name, used for
605	the `creates:` guard).

651	### 11. curl-installer (self-managed CLIs)
652	
653	Tools that ship via vendor `install.sh` instead of any package manager.
654	Mostly the AI coding agents (each vendor maintains their own installer
655	+ self-update subcommand). All landing paths are user-writable so
656	in-binary self-update works without sudo.
657	
658	**Inventory**:
659	
660	| Tool | Install URL | Lands at | Source role |
661	|---|---|---|---|
662	| Homebrew | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh` | `/usr/local/bin/brew` (macOS) / `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/` (Linux) | bootstrap |
663	| uv | `https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh` | `~/.local/bin/uv` (or `~/.cargo/bin/uv`) | bootstrap |
664	| mise | `https://mise.run` | `~/.local/bin/mise` | bootstrap |
665	| just | `https://just.systems/install.sh` | `/usr/local/bin/just` or `~/.local/bin/just` | `base` |
666	| starship | `https://starship.rs/install.sh` | `/usr/local/bin/starship` or `~/.local/bin/starship` | `starship` |
667	| atuin | `https://setup.atuin.sh` | `~/.atuin/bin/atuin` | `atuin` |
668	| docker | `https://get.docker.com` | system docker (rootless variant) | `docker` (Linux) |
669	| zoxide | (vendor installer) | `~/.local/bin/zoxide` | `devtools` (Linux fallback) |
670	| direnv | (vendor installer) | `~/.local/bin/direnv` | `devtools` (Linux fallback) |
671	| **Claude Code** | `https://claude.ai/install.sh` | `~/.claude/local/bin/claude` | `coding_agents` (Linux) |
672	| **OpenCode** | `https://opencode.ai/install` (+ `--no-modify-path`) | `~/.opencode/bin/opencode` | `coding_agents` (macOS + Linux) |
673	| **Cursor CLI** | `https://cursor.com/install` | `~/.local/bin/cursor-agent` | `coding_agents` |
674	| **Antigravity CLI** | `https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh` (patched `--skip-path --skip-aliases`) | `~/.local/bin/agy` + `agyc` symlink | `coding_agents` |
675	| **RTK** | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rtk-ai/rtk/master/install.sh` | `~/.local/bin/rtk` | `coding_agents` (Linux) |
676	| **llmfit** | `https://llmfit.axjns.dev/install.sh` | `~/.local/bin/llmfit` (or system) | `llm_tools` (Linux) |
677	| **Ollama** | `https://ollama.com/install.sh` | system path (Linux, sudo) | `llm_tools` (Linux) |
678	| Ookla speedtest | `https://install.speedtest.net/app/cli/install.<distro>.sh` | system | `networking_tools` (Linux) |
679	
680	**Why curl-installer over a package manager**:
681	
682	- Fast-moving releases — vendor controls cadence (Claude, OpenCode,
683	  Cursor, Antigravity push daily/weekly)
684	- Self-update subcommand exists and the installer is the canonical
685	  reinstall path → `cat_agents` in `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` can call
686	  either
687	- Avoids the "brew formula is 3 weeks stale" problem (see commit
688	  history for the OpenCode move from `anomalyco/tap` to official
689	  installer)
690	- No tap/PPA/repo to maintain
691	
692	**Adding a curl-installer tool**:
693	
694	1. Pick a role (or add to `coding_agents` if it's an agent)
695	2. Use the canonical pattern: `which` check → `creates:` guard on the
696	   binary path → `curl ... | bash [-s -- --no-modify-path]` shell task
697	3. If the installer mutates shell rc files, add a `--no-modify-path`
698	   flag (or equivalent — see OpenCode and Antigravity blocks). The
699	   chezmoi-managed PATH is the SSOT
700	4. Update `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_agents` if the tool has a
701	   self-update subcommand (or just an installer-as-upgrader path)
702	5. If the binary lands somewhere other than `~/.local/bin` (e.g.
703	   `~/.opencode/bin/opencode`), add an existence-gated PATH prepend
704	   to `dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl`
705	
706	### 12. GitHub-release downloads (user-level fallback)
707	
708	When apt/yum can't satisfy a version requirement (e.g. Apple Silicon
709	brew bottle missing, RHEL/CentOS package too old, noRoot host with no
710	sudo), roles fall back to downloading the latest GitHub release tarball
711	and extracting to `~/.local/bin` (user-writable, already on PATH).
712	
713	**Canonical pattern**:
714	
715	```yaml
716	- name: Get latest <tool> release
717	  ansible.builtin.uri:
718	    url: https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases/latest
719	    return_content: true
720	  register: <tool>_release
721	
722	- name: Compute <tool> arch
723	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
724	    <tool>_arch: "{{ 'amd64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64'] else 'arm64' if ... else 'unsupported' }}"
725	
726	- name: Download / extract / copy into ~/.local/bin
727	  block:
728	    - get_url: { url: "https://github.com/.../{{ tag }}/{{ asset }}", dest: /tmp/..., retries: 3, delay: 5, timeout: 120 }
729	    - unarchive: { src: ..., dest: /tmp/..., remote_src: true }
730	    - find:      { paths: /tmp/..., patterns: <binary>, file_type: file }
731	    - copy:      { src: ..., dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/<binary>", mode: '0755' }
732	  rescue:
733	    - debug: "<tool> installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"
734	```
735	
736	**Tools using this pattern** (rough list — see each role's `tasks/main.yml`):
737	
738	- `base`: `ripgrep`, `fd`, `jq`, `git-lfs`
739	- `devtools`: `gh`, `glab`, `bat`, `bats`, `eza`, `git-delta`, `diffnav`, `git-graph`, `glow`, `gum`, `vhs`, `freeze`, `duckdb`, `yazi`, `superfile`, `btop`, `zellij`, `sesh`, `worktrunk`, `workmux`, `taplo`, `tv` (television), `lnav`, `tailspin`, `dasel`, `yq`, `jnv`, `witr`
740	- `networking_tools`: `doggo`, `gping`, `trippy`, `bandwhich`, `rustscan`, `cloudflared`
741	- `neovim`: nvim tarball
742	- `lazyvim_deps`: `lazygit` fallback
743	- `coding_agents`: `specstory`, `codexbar`, `td`, `sidecar`, `agy` (all also have brew formula / cask as primary)
744	- `security_tools`: `gitleaks`
745	- `iac_tools`: `terraform`, `opentofu` user fallback (zip from `releases.hashicorp.com` / GitHub)
746	- `gui_apps_linux`: `AppImageLauncher Lite`, Zen Browser AppImage
747	- `bitwarden`: Desktop `.deb` fallback (Linux)
748	
749	**⚠️ Coverage gap**: GitHub-release downloads use a `creates:` guard
750	on the binary path, so once installed they're **never refreshed by
751	`chezmoi apply`** — and `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` has no category for
752	them. The only way to refresh: `rm` the binary, re-apply. See
753	[§ Coverage gaps](#coverage-gaps-install-only-no-automated-upgrade)
754	below.
755	
756	**Adding a GitHub-release tool**: copy the canonical block from
757	e.g. `devtools/tasks/main.yml` (look for an existing tool with a
758	similar arch matrix), substitute owner/repo/asset-name. Always wrap in
759	`block:` / `rescue:` (vendor-side outages happen) and use
760	`retries: 3, delay: 5, timeout: 120` on the download.
761	
762	### 13. chezmoi externals (refresh-periodic git/file fetches)
763	
764	**Config**: `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`
765	
766	`chezmoi apply` fetches these on a schedule. All set
767	`refreshPeriod = "168h"` (weekly), `--depth 1` clones, `--ff-only`
768	pulls.
769	
770	| Path | Type | Source | Gating |
771	|---|---|---|---|
772	| `.oh-my-zsh` | git-repo | `ohmyzsh/ohmyzsh.git` | always |
773	| `.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-autosuggestions` | git-repo | `zsh-users/zsh-autosuggestions.git` | always |
774	| `.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-syntax-highlighting` | git-repo | `zsh-users/zsh-syntax-highlighting.git` | always |
775	| `.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions` | git-repo | `zsh-users/zsh-completions.git` | always |
776	| `.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-vi-mode` | git-repo | `jeffreytse/zsh-vi-mode.git` | `enableVimMode` |
777	| `.oh-my-bash` | git-repo | `ohmybash/oh-my-bash.git` | always |
778	| `.local/src/blesh` | git-repo (`--recurse-submodules`) | `akinomyoga/ble.sh.git` | always; compiled by `run_onchange_after_26_install_blesh.sh.tmpl` → `~/.local/share/blesh/ble.sh` |
779	| `.tmux/plugins/tpm` | git-repo | `tmux-plugins/tpm.git` | always |
780	| `.fzf` | git-repo | `junegunn/fzf.git` | Linux only (ansible runs `~/.fzf/install --bin`) |
781	| `.local/share/toolkami/toolkami.rb` | file (executable) | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aperoc/toolkami/refs/heads/main/toolkami.rb` | always |
782	
783	**Why externals (not git clone in a role)**:
784	
785	- Refresh cadence is built-in (chezmoi handles `git pull` on schedule;
786	  ansible roles don't have a "re-pull every N hours" primitive)
787	- One place to see "what third-party source code lives on this machine"
788	- `chezmoi update --refresh-externals` is the explicit forced refresh
789	
790	**Upgrade**: `just upgrade-externals` → `chezmoi apply --refresh-externals`.
791	
792	**Adding an external**: prepend an entry to `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`.
793	If the cloned repo needs a post-clone compile step (like ble.sh),
794	attach a `run_onchange_after_NN_*.sh.tmpl` script that re-runs when
795	the external's commit changes.
796	
797	**Past pitfalls**:
798	
799	- ble.sh local-changes-overwritten ([`pitfalls/chezmoi-update-blesh-local-changes-overwritten.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/chezmoi-update-blesh-local-changes-overwritten.md)) — source clone moved out of the chezmoi external path to decouple from `make install`
800	
801	### 14. apt / yum (system packages)
802	
803	**The pragmatic Linux backbone**. Roles use apt/yum for tools that
804	are well-packaged by the distro (i.e. recent enough, available, no
805	notable upstream-vs-downstream skew).
806	
807	**Used by these roles** (non-exhaustive):
808

853	
854	### 15. ya pkg (Yazi plugins)
855	
856	Yazi's built-in plugin manager. `ya` (the yazi CLI companion) clones a plugin, copies it into `~/.config/yazi/plugins/`, and pins its revision in `~/.config/yazi/package.toml`.
857	
858	In this repo the **lockfile is chezmoi-managed** (`dot_config/yazi/package.toml`) and plugins are materialized by a hash-gated run-script, `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_45_yazi_plugins.sh.tmpl`, which runs `ya pkg install` whenever the lockfile changes. `ya pkg install` **rewrites** `package.toml` (normalizes it and strips comments), so the managed source lockfile is kept **comment-free** to match its canonical output — that's what avoids chezmoi drift (never add comments to it).
859	
860	| Plugin | Purpose |
861	|---|---|
862	| `yazi-rs/plugins:piper` (`piper.yazi`) | "pipe any shell command as a previewer" — backs the Office-document previewers in `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` (`piper -- view-office --preview …`) and the feather/sqlite preview fallbacks. See [office-viewers.md](../tools/office-viewers.md). |
863	| `wylie102/duckdb` (`duckdb.yazi`) | DuckDB-powered table previewer for data files (csv/tsv/parquet/xlsx/db/duckdb) — `run = "duckdb"` in `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` + required `require("duckdb"):setup{}` in `dot_config/yazi/init.lua`. Uses the `duckdb` CLI. See [data-viewers.md](../tools/data-viewers.md). |
864	
865	**Add a plugin:** `ya pkg add <owner>/<repo>:<plugin>`, then copy `~/.config/yazi/package.toml` back into the source. **Upgrade:** `ya pkg upgrade` → `just upgrade-yazi-plugins` (install-only by design; apply never bumps revs). Requires a recent yazi (`ya pkg` replaced the older `ya pack`).
866	
867	## Multi-mechanism tools + rationale
868	
869	Tools where the install path differs by OS / arch / role-feature-flag,
870	with rationale.
871	
872	| Tool | Mechanism dispatch | Why |
873	|---|---|---|
874	| **uv** | Bootstrap: curl. Later: dispatch between `brew upgrade uv` vs `uv self update` based on binary path | brew installs pin to versioned Cellar — `uv self update` no-ops there. Mirror logic in role + upgrade script keeps both paths working. See [pitfall](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md) |
875	| **OpenCode** | curl-installer on both OSes (2026-05) | Was brew tap (`anomalyco/tap`) on macOS, but formula version lagged + Cellar-pinning broke `opencode upgrade`. Unified on official installer with `--no-modify-path`. See `coding_agents/tasks/main.yml` `# === OpenCode` block |
876	| **OpenAI Codex CLI** | macOS: brew cask; Linux: npm `@openai/codex` | macOS has the brewed `.app` (richer); Linux only ships npm CLI |
877	| **Gemini CLI** | macOS: brew formula `gemini-cli` → npm fallback; Linux: npm | brew formula availability is inconsistent |
878	| **Specstory** | macOS: brew tap → GitHub release fallback; Linux: GitHub release tarball | brew formula availability + version freshness |
879	| **CodexBar** | macOS: brew tap (arm64 only); Linux: Linuxbrew → GitHub release | arm64-specific package |
880	| **td** / **sidecar** | macOS: brew tap; Linux: Linuxbrew → GitHub release | same maintainer (`marcus/tap`); Linuxbrew is fast path when present |
881	| **Ollama** | brew formula always (CLI); brew cask `ollama-app` when `installAiDesktopApps + installLlmTools`; Linux: `curl ollama.com/install.sh` | CLI vs GUI split; vendor installer is the canonical Linux path |
882	| **fzf** | macOS: `lazyvim_deps` brew. Linux: chezmoi external + `~/.fzf/install --bin` | brew is fine on macOS; Linux gets the latest git tip |
883	| **bash** | system bash always; homebrew bash 5.x only when `primary_shell="bash"` on macOS | macOS ships bash 3.2 (GPL2 vintage); brew bash 5 needed only if user actually wants it as login shell |
884	| **gh** | macOS: brew (via `devtools`); Linux: vendor apt repo → user tarball fallback | brew is canonical macOS; vendor apt repo is canonical Linux |
885	| **tmux** | macOS: brew; Linux: apt → `nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage` when system < 3.3 | `display-menu` popup requires 3.3+ — see AGENTS.md tmux hard invariant |
886	| **Discord** | macOS: brew cask; Linux: flatpak (default) or `.deb` via `discordChannel` chooser | apt has no Discord; flatpak is sandboxed-and-current, `.deb` is for users who hate flatpak |
887	| **Steam** | macOS: brew cask gated by `installGamingApps`; Linux: Valve apt repo + `steam-launcher` gated by `installGamingApps` | Valve's apt repo is the supported Linux path; Flathub exists but is community-packaged |
888	| **just**, **starship**, **zoxide**, **direnv** | macOS: brew; Linux: vendor curl-installer | Linux distro packages are too stale for these fast-moving tools |
889	| **Neovim** | macOS: brew (`state: latest`); Linux: apt → GitHub release tarball → user fallback → `neovim/neovim-releases` on oldEL | Min version 0.11.2 is too new for most distros; no snap by policy |
890	| **tree-sitter-cli** | npm via mise (preferred, timeout 180) → cargo fallback | npm is faster; cargo needs libclang to compile. Same binary either way |
891	| **bw (Bitwarden CLI)** | npm global (preferred) or system npm fallback | always npm, the dispatch is mise-npm vs system-npm |
892	
893	**Adding a tool with multi-mechanism dispatch**: prefer ONE primary
894	mechanism per OS, with at most ONE fallback. Multiple fallbacks add
895	test combinations (5 levels × 5 OS variants = 25 cells) that nobody
896	will actually exercise. If you can't decide, write the simplest version
897	and add fallbacks only when an actual host fails.
898	
899	---
900	
901	## Fallback chains
902	
903	Notable cascading-fallback patterns:
904	
905	| Tool | Chain |
906	|---|---|
907	| **mise binary** | curl `https://mise.run` (preferred) → direct binary download from `mise.jdx.dev/mise-latest-linux-${arch}` → musl variant (forced when glibc < 2.28) |
908	| **Neovim (Linux)** | apt → GitHub release tarball when too old (`/opt/nvim` + symlink) → user-tarball to `~/.local` → `neovim-releases` fork (oldEL glibc 2.17 rebuild) |
909	| **Most Linux CLIs in base/devtools/networking_tools** | apt/yum (sudo) → user-level GitHub release musl tarball to `~/.local/bin`. Several have arch-specific brew-on-aarch64 branch (`eza`, `git-delta`) |
910	| **Rust (mise)** | configured mirror → official `static.rust-lang.org` → on oldEL: `rustup-init` directly |
911	| **Cursor `.deb` (Linux)** | `get_url` with retries=4 (large file, GFW-prone) — single mechanism but heavily retried |
912	| **Bitwarden Desktop (Linux)** | snap → `.deb` fallback |
913	| **CodexBar / td / sidecar / RTK / specstory / llmfit** | Linuxbrew → GitHub release tarball |
914	| **uv (upgrade-side)** | inspect binary path → `brew upgrade uv` or `uv self update` |
915	| **Discord (Linux)** | flatpak (default) → `.deb` (selectable via `discordChannel`) |
916	| **tree-sitter-cli (Linux)** | `mise exec -- npm install -g tree-sitter-cli` (timeout 180) → `cargo install tree-sitter-cli` (installs `libclang-dev` first) |
917	| **Antigravity installer** | curl → `sed` patch in-flight to inject `--skip-path --skip-aliases` → bash (avoids profile mutation) |
918	| **just** | macOS brew → Linux: vendor `curl install.sh` with `sudo` → user-level `--bin-dir ~/.local/bin` fallback |
919	
920	**Why fallbacks**: noRoot Linux hosts, RHEL/CentOS 7 (glibc 2.17, no
921	modern bottles, ancient zsh), Apple Silicon Macs (some brew formulae
922	have no arm64 bottle), Chinese-mirror outages.

1	# dotfiles
2	
3	Cross-platform development environment setup using **chezmoi** + **ansible**.
4	
5	- **chezmoi**: manages config files (dotfiles)
6	- **ansible**: installs system dependencies and tools
7	
8	> **Native Windows?** This repo covers macOS, Linux, and WSL. For a native
9	> Windows + PowerShell 7 setup (scoop + winget, starship, `copilot-proxy`), use
10	> **[dotfiles-windows](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles-windows)**.
11	
12	## Prerequisites
13	
14	- [chezmoi](https://www.chezmoi.io/install/)
15	- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) (for ansible)
16	
17	## Architecture

59	
60	## Quick Setup
61	
62	### Interactive (recommended)
63	
64	```bash
65	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh | bash
66	```
67	
68	Installs [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (if missing) and launches `dotfiles-init` — a Python wrapper that groups the ~19 chezmoi prompts into a clean multi-select UI, offers pre-set bundles (`personal-mac` / `work-mac` / `server-linux` / `cloud-vm` / `minimal`), checks SSH keys, then calls real `chezmoi init` with your answers pre-filled. Full docs: [`scripts/init/README.md`](scripts/init/README.md).
69	
70	On first-run or slow networks the `uv` resolver can sit silently for a few minutes — use the verbose form to see timestamped progress + `uv --verbose` resolver output + `set -x`:
71	
72	```bash
73	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh | DOTFILES_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE=1 bash
74	```
75	
76	Pass extra args through to the wrapper via `bash -s --` (e.g. run the schema-parity checker instead of the default `init`):
77	
78	```bash
79	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh | bash -s -- doctor
80	```
81	
82	Behind GFW? Set `DOTFILES_RAW_URL` / `DOTFILES_REF` to point at a mirror, or use the non-interactive path below.
83	
84	### Non-interactive (direct chezmoi)
85	
86	```bash
87	# Installs chezmoi to ~/.local/bin and walks through the raw prompts one-by-one.
88	# Uses HTTPS to avoid SSH key setup on fresh machines.
89	export GITHUB_USERNAME=daviddwlee84
90	sh -c "$(curl -fsLS get.chezmoi.io)" -- -b "$HOME/.local/bin" init --apply "https://github.com/$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git"
91	
92	# After install, switch the chezmoi source repo to SSH (so future `chezmoi update` uses your SSH key):
93	#   chezmoi cd
94	#   git remote set-url origin git@github.com:$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git
95	#   exit
96	```
97	
98	This automatically:
99	
100	1. Bootstraps Homebrew (macOS/Linux), uv, mise, ansible
101	2. Deploys all config files
102	3. Runs ansible playbooks (git, ripgrep, fd, neovim, etc.)
103	4. Runs brew bundle (if `installBrewApps` is enabled, or on macOS if `installAiDesktopApps` / `installGamingApps` is enabled)
104	
105	#### Sudo password injection (when chezmoi can't open `/dev/tty`)
106	
107	Some Linux environments — notably **CentOS 7 + AD/LDAP user with high UID** where `pam_systemd` never created `/run/user/<UID>/` — leave the chezmoi-spawned bootstrap script unable to open `/dev/tty`, so the shared sudo helper can't prompt and Linuxbrew aborts with `Insufficient permissions to install Homebrew to "/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew"`. The fix is to pre-stage the password via `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (the same env-var [`fleet_apply`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md) uses over SSH).
108	
109	The repo ships [`scripts/apply_with_sudo.sh`](scripts/apply_with_sudo.sh) to handle the prompt → 0600 tmpfile → export → run → `shred` dance:
110	
111	```bash
112	# First time (chezmoi not installed yet):
113	sh -c "$(curl -fsLS get.chezmoi.io)" -- -b "$HOME/.local/bin"   # install chezmoi only
114	bash <(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles/main/scripts/apply_with_sudo.sh) \
115	  --init "https://github.com/$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git"
116	
117	# Re-runs (after chezmoi source is cloned at ~/.local/share/chezmoi):
118	just apply-with-sudo                                              # interactive prompt
119	just apply-with-sudo --pass-from-env                              # reads $SUDO_PASSWORD
120	SUDO_PASSWORD=xxx just apply-with-sudo --pass-from-env            # one-liner
121	```
122	
123	The wrapper validates the password against `sudo -v` before invoking `chezmoi`, then shreds the tmpfile on exit (any signal). Inside chezmoi's run-scripts, `sudo_session_init` adopts the file, moves it into the shared state dir, and spawns the watchdog that keeps the sudo timestamp warm.
124	
125	**Even simpler alternative** if you have root and don't mind editing sudoers: add `$USER ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL` to `/etc/sudoers.d/99-bootstrap`, run `chezmoi apply`, then remove the line. The shared helper short-circuits cleanly when sudo is truly passwordless.
126	
127	> CentOS 7 also blocks Linuxbrew install because system curl 7.29 is older than Homebrew's 7.41 minimum, and Homebrew bottles built on Ubuntu 22.04+ don't run on glibc 2.17 anyway. Linuxbrew is fully optional on Linux — every ansible task that uses it has a non-brew fallback (cargo / GitHub musl release / AppImage). On CentOS 7, drop a stub `~/.local/bin/brew` (`#!/bin/sh\nexit 0`) before applying to short-circuit the bootstrap's brew step.
128	
129	Full diagnosis: [`pitfalls/bootstrap-no-tty-sudo-prompt-skipped.md`](pitfalls/bootstrap-no-tty-sudo-prompt-skipped.md) and [`pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md`](pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md).
130	
131	### After install
132	
133	- `~/.local/bin` and the rest of the shared layer (mise/uv/cargo/bun PATH, plus Linux OpenCode's `~/.opencode/bin`) are exported via `~/.config/shell/00_exports.sh`, sourced by both the chezmoi-managed `~/.bashrc` and `~/.zshrc`.
134	- On sudo-enabled machines, the ansible role for your `primaryShell` choice switches your login shell automatically (`zsh` role for `primaryShell=zsh`, `bash` role for `primaryShell=bash`). Log out / back in to pick it up, or run `exec zsh` / `exec bash` now.
135	- `primaryShell=bash` on macOS additionally installs Homebrew bash 5.x and adds it to `/etc/shells` (system bash 3.2 is too old for oh-my-bash plugins + ble.sh). zsh-primary mac users see no extra brew install.
136	- On `noRoot=true` installs, login shell isn't changed — run `exec zsh` / `exec bash` per session, or ask your sysadmin: `sudo chsh -s "$(command -v zsh)" $USER` (or `bash`).
137	- Open a new shell after install so PATH changes take effect. Both `~/.bashrc` and `~/.zshrc` are deployed regardless of `primaryShell` choice, so the other shell still works ad-hoc.

165	| `installCalibre` | false | [calibre](https://calibre-ebook.com/) e-book toolkit (`ebook-meta`/`ebook-convert`). Enables Kindle `.mobi`/`.azw`/`.azw3` metadata previews in yazi via `view-ebook` (see [yazi-previews.md](docs/tools/yazi-previews.md)). Heavy GUI app (~hundreds of MB); the preview is best-effort and also works if calibre is already installed by hand. |
166	| `installDotnetTools` | false | .NET SDK via mise + dotnet global tools ([azure-cost-cli](docs/tools/dotnet-tools.md) for Azure cost analysis) |
167	| `installExtraRuntimes` | true | Extra mise runtimes (rust, bun, ruby, go; ~1.8GB) + their cargo/gem/go tool roles. Node is always installed regardless. Set false for lean cloud VMs / CI. |
168	| `installAuditd` | false | Linux audit framework (auditd) + baseline rules (identity / sudoers / sshd_config / privileged-exec). Linux only. See [docs/sysadmin/auditd.md](docs/sysadmin/auditd.md). |
169	| `installHomelabTools` | false | Homelab hardware-monitoring CLIs (lm-sensors, smartmontools, ipmitool, nvme-cli, storcli) + `hw-*` shell helpers, each gated on detected hardware. Linux only; no-op in VMs. See [docs/sysadmin/hardware.md](docs/sysadmin/hardware.md). |
170	| `installResilioSync` | false | [Resilio Sync](https://www.resilio.com/sync/) P2P file sync (AirDrop-style transfer, phone→NAS photo backup). macOS: GUI app via Homebrew cask. Linux (desktop + server): headless daemon (no GUI) as a per-user systemd service, WebUI at `127.0.0.1:8888`. See [docs/tools/resilio-sync.md](docs/tools/resilio-sync.md). |
171	| `installWakeOnLan` | false | Wake-on-LAN (passive side): arm this box's wired NIC(s) to power on from a magic packet, persisted across reboots via a `wol@<iface>` systemd unit (installs ethtool). Linux only; no-op in VMs. Wake-from-S5 also needs BIOS "Power On By PCI-E" on + "ErP Ready" off. Sender side = the `wake` CLI / `wakeonlan`. See [docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md](docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md). |
172	| `useChineseMirror` | false | Switch Homebrew / pip / npm / cargo / etc. to China (GFW) mirrors |
173	| `gitleaksAllRepos` | false | Run gitleaks on ALL git repos, not just those with `.pre-commit-config.yaml` |
174	| `backupMode` | `smart` | Back up existing dotfiles before apply: `smart` (only files chezmoi overwrites), `full` (fixed allowlist), `off` (skip) |
175	| `allowPartialFailure` | false | Continue installing other Ansible roles if one role fails |
176	| `noRoot` | false | Skip sudo-requiring tasks (for servers without root access). Linux only. |
177	| `motdStyle` | `figlet` | SSH login banner style: `figlet` (~6 lines, default), `fastfetch-slim` (figlet + fastfetch w/o logo, ~10 lines), `fastfetch-full` (full distro logo + everything, ~22 lines). Runtime override: `MOTD_STYLE=...` in `~/.zshrc.adhoc`. See [docs/zsh/motd.md](docs/zsh/motd.md). |
178	| `primaryShell` | `zsh` | Primary interactive shell: `zsh` (default, full-featured) or `bash` (oh-my-bash + ble.sh, close-to-zsh UX). Both `~/.zshrc` and `~/.bashrc` deploy on every host; this only governs which shell `chsh` switches to as the login shell. See [docs/shells/bash.md](docs/shells/bash.md) for the bash side's known gaps and tradeoffs. |
179	| `enableVimMode` | true | Vim-style modal editing in shells (zsh-vi-mode, `set -o vi`, ble.sh) + tmux vim navigation. Does NOT affect Neovim. See [docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md). |
180	<!-- /dotfiles-init:prompts -->
181	
182	To change options later, don't hand-edit `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml` — run the reconfigure tool, which seeds the same TUI from your current values and re-applies via `chezmoi init --apply --prompt`:
183	
184	```bash
185	just reconfigure                 # interactive (or: czcfg)
186	just reconfigure -- --set installLlmTools=true --yes   # non-interactive single key
187	```
188	
189	See [`scripts/init/README.md`](scripts/init/README.md) → "Reconfigure".

191	## What You Get
192	
193	### Config Files
194	
195	- `~/.gitconfig` - Git configuration; managed via `modify_` so `gh auth setup-git`'s `[credential "..."]` blocks (with the per-machine absolute path to `gh`) survive `chezmoi apply`; default pull behavior is rebase + autostash (`pull.rebase=true`, `rebase.autoStash=true`) so LazyGit's `p` pull keeps local dirty work across the rebase ([docs](docs/tools/gh-cli.md), [LazyGit notes](docs/tools/lazygit.md))
196	- `~/.config/git/hooks/` - Global Git hooks (via a global `core.hooksPath`): managed `pre-commit` (gitleaks) + Git LFS hooks, all hardened to skip gracefully — PATH-robust and non-fatal so a stripped-PATH clone like `brew tap` can't break (see [pitfall](pitfalls/git-lfs-global-hook-breaks-brew-tap.md))
197	- `~/.config/gh-dash/config.yml` - Global gh-dash config, with `diffnav` as the diff pager
198	- `~/.config/lazygit/config.yml` - Global LazyGit config, with `delta` as the custom diff pager
199	- `~/.config/bat/themes/tokyonight_night.tmTheme` - Managed Tokyo Night theme for bat; apply rebuilds the bat cache and clears it if the cache is incompatible with `delta`
200	- `~/.config/nvim/` - Neovim (LazyVim) configuration; system clipboard via `unnamedplus`, with an SSH-conditional OSC 52 override so remote yanks reach the local clipboard (pairs with tmux `set-clipboard on`, see [docs](docs/tools/tmux/README.md#osc-52-clipboard-ssh-friendly-yank))
201	- `~/.config/uv/uv.toml` - uv package manager config (PyPI: official / Aliyun+TUNA+USTC via `useChineseMirror`)
202	- `~/.cargo/config.toml` - Cargo registry config (crates.io / TUNA sparse index via `useChineseMirror`)
203	- `~/.npmrc` - npm registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
204	- `~/.config/.bunfig.toml` - Bun global registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
205	- `~/.gemrc` - RubyGems source + common options (TUNA mirror; only managed when `useChineseMirror=true`, gated via `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`)
206	- `~/.condarc` - Conda/Mamba channels with TUNA Anaconda mirror (only managed when `useChineseMirror=true`, preserves `auto_activate_base`/user channel prefs)
207	- `~/.config/zsh/00_exports.zsh` - Env-var mirror bundle (Homebrew / Rustup / mise / GOPROXY) when `useChineseMirror=true`; also exported by bootstrap + ansible runner scripts so first-run installs and ansible subprocesses inherit them ([docs](docs/tools/mirrors.md))
208	- `~/.config/zsh/99_local_proxy.zsh` - Create-only machine-local proxy override stub; uncomment `LOCAL_PROXY_URL` / `LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL` here to pin Clash ports without future chezmoi diffs
209	- `~/.docker/config.json` - Docker client `proxies.default` block (auto-injected from `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` / `$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL`; preserves `auths` / `credsStore` via chezmoi modify-script) ([docs](docs/tools/containers.md))
210	- `~/.config/docker/daemon.json` - Rootless Docker `registry-mirrors` (DaoCloud / USTC / NJU / ...; Linux + `useChineseMirror` only) ([docs](docs/tools/containers.md#strategy-a-registry-mirrors-in-daemonjson))
211	- `~/.config/alacritty/` - Alacritty terminal config (CSI-u keybindings for `Ctrl+Number` tmux window switching, `option_as_alt` for Meta keys)
212	- `~/Library/Application Support/{Code,Cursor,Antigravity}/User/` (macOS) + `~/.config/{Code,Cursor,Antigravity}/User/` (Linux) - Editor settings overlay: `modify_settings.json` deep-merges a 6-key baseline (Hack Nerd Font Mono, relative line numbers, format on save, smart-accept suggestion, terminal font) into each editor's live `settings.json` without overwriting other keys; `create_keybindings.json` seeds 5 universal keybindings on a fresh machine and never overwrites editor-added entries. Canonical templates live under [`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`](.chezmoitemplates/editor/); `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` gates each editor dir with a `stat` presence check so uninstalled editors never produce phantom directories.
213	- `~/.config/ghostty/config` - Ghostty/cmux terminal config (`macos-option-as-alt` for tmux Meta keybindings, disabled ligatures, explicit `clipboard-write = allow` / `clipboard-read = ask` for OSC 52) ([docs](docs/tools/ghostty.md))
214	- `~/.config/starship.toml` - Starship cross-shell prompt config
215	- `~/.xonshrc` + `~/.config/xonsh/rc.xsh` - Optional [Xonsh](https://xon.sh/) (Python-superset shell) startup + extension sandbox. Installed via `python_uv_tools` with a curated set of xontribs (`jedi`/`zoxide`/`pipeliner`/`fzf-widgets`); **not** a login shell — drop in with `xonsh` for ad-hoc Python-in-shell work ([docs](docs/shells/xonsh.md))
216	- `~/.config/direnv/direnvrc` - direnv helper functions, including `.venv`-aware Python activation
217	- `~/.config/yazi/` - Yazi file manager config (v0.3.3+ syntax, [docs](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/configuration/overview/))
218	  - `yazi.toml` - Main config with open rules and openers (`o`/`O`)
219	  - `keymap.toml`, `theme.toml` - Optional customization files (stubs provided)
220	- `~/.config/btop/btop.conf` + `~/.config/btop/themes/catppuccin_mocha.theme` - btop system-monitor baseline (Catppuccin Mocha theme, process tree view, `vim_keys` mirrors `enableVimMode`); seeded once via `create_` so btop's on-exit config rewrites never cause chezmoi drift; catppuccin theme vendored like bat's ([docs](docs/tools/btop.md))
221	- `~/.claude/` - Claude Code settings
222	- `~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml` - Coding-agent CLI overlays: each `modify_*` script deep-merges a small managed baseline (preferences, features, curated plugins) into the CLI's live config, preserving auth tokens, per-project trust, sessions, and other machine-local state. Codex specifically round-trips `[projects]` and `[marketplaces.*]` so per-project trust paths never get clobbered. OpenCode legacy `~/.config/opencode/config.json` is migrated to the modern filename by a one-shot `run_once_before_50_opencode_migrate.sh.tmpl`. Full design: [docs/tools/agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
223	- `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml` - Global SpecStory defaults for `specstory run` across all projects
224	- `~/.tmux.conf` - Tmux configuration with TPM plugins (resurrect, continuum, tmux-floax floating pane, tmux-fzf for fuzzy keybinding/session/pane search rebound to `prefix+?`, tmux-fzf-url, tmux-open), vim-style copy mode with clipboard yank, capture-pane helpers (`prefix+y`/`Y`/`C-y`), a native popup menu (`prefix+Space` or `prefix+e`, script-driven with submenus and height-aware trimming) with layout/resize/session management, popup shell (`prefix+\``) and lazygit popup (`prefix+G`), a glow-rendered cheatsheet (`prefix+Space` → `?`), vim-style pane nav, `Ctrl+1..9` quick window switching (CSI-u terminals), extended-keys for coding agents (including `Ctrl+/` in Neovim), sesh keybindings (`prefix+g` fzf picker, `prefix+T` television picker, `prefix+O` built-in picker, `prefix+W` window picker, `prefix+S` last), responsive Catppuccin status bar (adapts modules to terminal width for mobile), and config reload on `prefix+R` ([docs](docs/tools/tmux/README.md))
225	- `~/.dotfiles/bin/x` - Cross-platform terminal wrapper for `copy` / `copy-file` / `paste` / `open`; `x copy` has an OSC 52 fallback for SSH text copy, while `x copy-file` copies desktop file objects for Finder / Files paste ([docs](docs/tools/clipboard.md))
226	- `~/.dotfiles/bin/sms` - Huawei router SMS reader (HiLink XML API; verification-code extraction, clipboard integration, TV channel) ([docs](docs/tools/sms.md))
227	- `~/.config/sms/config.toml.example` - Starter config for the `sms` CLI (real `config.toml` is created at runtime, never committed)
228	- `~/.config/television/cable/sms.toml` - Television channel for browsing router SMS inbox
229	- `~/.dotfiles/bin/mi-router` - Read-only inspector for Xiaomi / MiWiFi routers (LuCI JSON API; `info`/`wifi`/`devices`/`mdns`/`raw` subcommands; sister tool to `sms`) ([docs](docs/tools/mi-router.md))
230	- `~/.config/mi-router/config.toml.example` - Starter config for the `mi-router` CLI (real `config.toml` is created at runtime, never committed)
231	- `~/.config/sesh/sesh.toml` - Sesh session manager config (named sessions with windows, wildcards, defaults) ([docs](docs/tools/sesh.md))
232	- `~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml` - Worktrunk (`wt`) git-worktree manager config — aliases (`wt sw`/`ls`/`rm`/`cc`/`oc`); hooks & LLM commit generation kept commented as opt-in ([workflow playbook](docs/tools/worktrunk.md))
233	- `~/.config/workmux/config.yaml` - Workmux (`wm`) git-worktree + agent status orchestrator — `nerdfont:false` + `status_format:false` (we self-manage the tmux format in `theme.catppuccin.conf`); 🤖/💬/✅ icons fed by Claude/OpenCode hooks ([playbook](docs/tools/workmux.md))
234	- `~/.config/television/cable/sesh.toml` - Television custom cable channel for sesh (overrides built-in with richer sources and actions)
235	- `~/.config/television/cable/lan-devices.toml` + `~/.config/television/lan-scan.sh` - Television channel for LAN device discovery with open ports, MAC/vendor, hostname, RTT; streams results incrementally via a cache file ([docs](docs/tools/tv.md))
236	- `~/.config/television/cable/azure.toml` + `~/.config/television/azure-{source,preview,rotate-ip}.sh` - Television channel for Azure resources (Resource Groups / VMs / Public IPs / NICs+NSGs / all) with VM actions (restart, start/stop, deallocate, rotate public IP, SSH, open in portal) and graceful login prompt ([docs](docs/tools/tv.md))
237	- `~/.config/television/cable/clash.toml` + `~/.config/television/clash-switch.sh` - YAML-backed Clash / mihomo Television channel; auto-resolves Clash's active `profiles/<time>.yml` from `~/.config/clash/profiles/list.yml`, falls back to legacy `config.{yaml,yml}`, supports proxy-group switching, and turns empty proxies/groups/rules tabs into informative placeholder rows instead of blank panes ([docs](docs/tools/tv.md))
238	- `~/.config/television/cable/clash-api.toml` + `~/.config/television/clash-switch.sh` - Live Clash external-controller Television channel for `/proxies`, `/rules`, `/configs`, and `/connections`; supports remote controllers via `CLASH_CONTROLLER` / `CLASH_SECRET` and proxy-group switching without adding an in-UI host switch ([docs](docs/tools/tv.md))
239	- `~/.config/television/cable/logs.toml` - Television channel for fuzzy-browsing log files with tailspin/bat previews, `Enter` opens in `lnav`, `Alt+T` live tails with tailspin ([docs](docs/tools/log-tools.md))
240	- `~/.config/television/cable/services.toml` - Cross-platform services channel for systemd (Linux) / launchd (macOS) — 5 source cycles (running/all/failed/user-scope/installed-on-disk), tailspin log preview, Alt-key lifecycle actions (restart/stop/start/reload/enable), sudo-aware ([docs](docs/tools/services.md))
241	- `~/.config/television/cable/skills.toml` + `~/.config/television/cable/skills-walk.toml` - Two Television channels for browsing agent skills: `skills` parses `npx skills list` (project + global, with Agents column), `skills-walk` walks `~/.agents/`, `~/.claude/`, `~/.codex/`, `~/.cursor/skills-cursor/` directly without invoking npx; both preview SKILL.md with bat
242	- `~/.config/television/cable/agent-sessions.toml` + `~/.config/television/agent-sessions.py` - Unified Television channel for coding-agent sessions across OpenCode (SQLite), Claude Code (JSONL), Codex (JSONL), Cursor Agent CLI (store.db), and Cursor IDE composer chats (state.vscdb); 6 source cycles (all/per-agent), content-searchable via first-user-message snippet, `Enter` prints `cd <dir> && <agent> --resume <id>`, `Alt+T` resumes in current shell (Cursor IDE: opens workspace folder via `cursor <dir>` since IDE has no chat-resume CLI flag)
243	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh` + `03_tmux_capture.zsh` + `04_ai_capture.zsh` - **aicapture** layer: OSC 133 prompt markers + `cpout`/`cpcmd`/`cpblock [N]` scrollback helpers + `aifix`/`aiexplain` LLM wrappers (advisory-only; Haiku/mini by default) + `aiblock` Python TUI (multi-select + spawn agent window). Full guide: [docs/tools/aicapture.md](docs/tools/aicapture.md); design-space comparison against thefuck/Warp/wut/tmuxai/atuin in [docs/this_repo/instant-llm-fix-prior-art.md](docs/this_repo/instant-llm-fix-prior-art.md)
244	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/05_aisuggest.zsh` - **aisuggest** prompt-time NL→shell ghost text. Type a description, press `Alt+;`, see the suggested command, Tab to accept. Routes through the same `_aiagent_invoke` autodetect (claude → opencode → codex → cursor-agent) — no API key needed. Inspired by [`kylesnowschwartz/zsh-ai-cmd`](https://github.com/kylesnowschwartz/zsh-ai-cmd); architecture in [docs/tools/zsh-inline-ai.md](docs/tools/zsh-inline-ai.md)
245	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/22_sesh.zsh` - Sesh keybinding (`Alt+S` for session picker), `shere`/`sroot` session helpers (supports bare command args, e.g. `shere specstory run codex`), and shell completion

247	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/41_github.zsh` - GitHub helper with `ghget` for downloading a repo subdirectory from a tree URL
248	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh` - Networking aliases plus loopback proxy helpers (`proxy-on`, `proxy-off`, `proxy-status`, `proxy-test`, `withproxy`) that prefer `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL`, then Clash's active config, then loopback port probing
249	- `~/.config/shell/37_lazygit.sh` - LazyGit shell alias: `lg` (shared by zsh/bash)

251	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/29_log_tools.zsh` - Log viewer wrappers: `catl` (tspin colorful cat), `lessl` (ccze + less), `logtail` (tspin live follow) ([docs](docs/tools/log-tools.md))

Catppuccin theme, tmux-like keybindings, `tv`/lazygit command-panes, herdr-plus Projects layouts, and native agent-state indicators. 272	### Upstream Clones (via `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`)
273	
274	Vendored upstream sources are declared in [`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`](.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl) and auto-refreshed weekly by chezmoi (`refreshPeriod = "168h"`). Force an immediate pull with `chezmoi apply --refresh-externals`.

277	- `~/.tmux/plugins/tpm` (TPM)
278	- `~/.fzf` (Linux only; apt version lacks `--zsh`)
279	- `~/.local/share/toolkami/toolkami.rb`

283	### Tools (via ansible)
284	
285	- **Base**: git, git-lfs, curl, ripgrep, fd, just, build tools
286	- **Neovim**: >= 0.11.2 with LazyVim dependencies
287	- **LazyVim deps**: fzf, lazygit, tree-sitter-cli, Node.js
288	- **Git review stack**: gh, glab, gh-dash (via `gh` extension), diffnav, git-delta, lazygit
289	- **Markdown reader**: `glow` for terminal Markdown rendering, plus `readurl <url>` / `readlocal` / `readnode` / `readraw` to render web pages as markdown in the terminal with auto proxy fallback (see [docs/tools/web-reader.md](docs/tools/web-reader.md))
290	- **Office documents**: view Word/Excel/PowerPoint (plus legacy `.doc/.xls/.ppt` and OpenDocument) in the terminal via the `view-office` dispatcher — [doxx](https://github.com/bgreenwell/doxx) (docx), visidata (xlsx), [markitdown](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown) (pptx), LibreOffice headless fallback; also wired as a [yazi](docs/tools/office-viewers.md) inline previewer (see [docs/tools/office-viewers.md](docs/tools/office-viewers.md))
291	- **Data files**: preview CSV/TSV/Parquet/Feather/Excel/SQLite as aligned tables inline in [yazi](docs/tools/data-viewers.md) via the [duckdb.yazi](https://github.com/wylie102/duckdb.yazi) plugin (DuckDB `-box`) + VisiData fallback for Feather; explore interactively with [VisiData](https://www.visidata.org/) `vd` (see [docs/tools/data-viewers.md](docs/tools/data-viewers.md))

356	## Keeping tools up-to-date
357	
358	`chezmoi apply` is deliberately **install-only** — ansible roles mostly use
359	`state: present` / `creates:` idempotency so re-applying never silently bumps
360	every tool on your machine. For explicit upgrades, use the dedicated entry
361	points (see [`docs/this_repo/upgrades.md`](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md) for the full matrix):
362	
363	```bash
364	just upgrade-all          # externals + brew + mise + uv + npm + cargo + go + dotnet + gem + agents + plugins
365	just upgrade-dry-run      # preview without executing
366	
367	# Per category (compose as you like):
368	just upgrade-brew         # formulas + casks (--greedy) + Brewfile (no --no-upgrade) + cleanup
369	just upgrade-mise         # mise self-update + `mise upgrade`
370	just upgrade-uv           # uv itself (auto-dispatches: brew vs self update) + `uv tool upgrade --all` (apprise, mlflow, sqlit-tui, ...)
371	just upgrade-npm          # global npm packages (Bitwarden CLI, readability-cli, ...)
372	just upgrade-cargo        # cargo install-update -a (bootstraps cargo-update)
373	just upgrade-go           # go install <pkg>@latest per go_tools entry (Linux only; on macOS translate → brew)
374	just upgrade-dotnet       # .NET global tools (azure-cost-cli, ...)
375	just upgrade-gem          # Ruby gems (try-cli, tmuxinator, ...)
376	just upgrade-agents       # re-runs install.sh for Claude Code / OpenCode / Cursor CLI / Ollama / llmfit / RTK
377	just upgrade-plugins      # LazyVim :Lazy sync + TPM + claude-hud + pre-commit autoupdate + tldr + gh extensions
378	just upgrade-externals    # chezmoi upgrade + chezmoi apply --refresh-externals
379	```
380	
381	Underlying script: [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) —
382	best-effort, prints a `SUCCESS / SKIPPED / FAILED` summary at the end. Full
383	docs, rationale, run-order diagram, and extension guide live in
384	[docs/this_repo/upgrades.md](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md).
385	
386	When installed, `just upgrade-plugins` also refreshes `claude-hud` to the
387	latest upstream release. Upstream `claude-hud` `v0.0.12+` now follows Claude
388	Code's official stdin `rate_limits` only, so the old credential-derived `Max`
389	plan badge may disappear after upgrade.
390	
391	## Multi-host apply (`just fleet-apply`)
392	
393	Push the same `chezmoi update --init` to every host in
394	`~/.config/fleet/machines.toml`, in parallel, with sudo password sourced from
395	plaintext / interactive prompt / Bitwarden CLI:
396	
397	```bash
398	just fleet-edit                      # edit ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml ($EDITOR)
399	just fleet-status                    # pre-flight readiness probe (read-only, ~1.5s/host)
400	just fleet-apply                     # parallel, all hosts (chezmoi update --init)
401	just fleet-apply-dry-run             # `chezmoi diff` on each host (no changes)
402	just fleet-apply-one lab-box         # single host, --serial mode (debug)
403	```
404	
405	Connection prefers `~/.ssh/config` aliases (`ProxyJump`, `IdentityAgent`,
406	etc. all inherited) and falls back to explicit `hostname/user/port/identity_file`.
407	Per-host log: `logs/fleet-apply/<UTC-timestamp>/<host>.log`. Exit code = number
408	of failed hosts. Inventory file is seeded once by chezmoi as a
409	`create_private_` template, so your edits are never overwritten.
410	
411	`fleet-status` is the recommended pre-apply gate — it predicts what `fleet-apply`
412	would do per host (`up-to-date` / `behind` / `drift` / `busy` /
413	`toml-mismatch` / `not-init` / `unreachable` / ...) without changing
414	anything, and prints actionable hints for each non-green state. See
415	[docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md § Readiness probe](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md#readiness-probe-just-fleet-status)
416	for the full state matrix.
417	
418	Conflict-handling defaults match the "push canonical config" mental model:
419	`--keep-going` is **on** (skip drifted files non-destructively, continue
420	the rest), `--force` is **off** (don't auto-overwrite). Pass
421	`--no-keep-going` to fail-fast, or `--force` to silently overwrite local
422	drift on the remote — see [docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md)
423	for the full flag reference and per-machine git override convention
424	(`~/.gitconfig.local`, same self-managed pattern as `~/.zshrc.adhoc`).
425	
426	## Testing
427	
428	Two layers, both opt-in — this is a personal dotfiles repo, tests only cover painful-regression zones:
429	
430	- **`just bats`** — fast unit tests (no Docker, no network). Covers proxy helpers (`tests/unit/zsh_proxy.bats`), `ghget` URL parsing (`tests/unit/ghget.bats`), and `lan-scan.sh` pure helpers (`tests/unit/lan_scan.bats`).
431	- **`just docker-test`** — smoke tests in a clean Ubuntu container: re-apply idempotency, zsh config parses, `oh-my-zsh` plugins present, core CLI tools on PATH, nested unit tests pass under Ubuntu zsh (`tests/smoke/docker_install.bats`).
432	- **`just docker-test-centos7` / `just docker-test-rocky9`** — same smoke suite under the `centos_server` profile. CentOS 7 covers the legacy glibc-2.17 noRoot corporate target (see [`pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md`](pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md)); Rocky 9 covers the modern dnf-native RHEL-family path. `just docker-test-centos-all` runs both.
433	- **`just check-all`** — everything: ansible syntax + pre-commit + `bats` + `docker-test`.
434	
435	`shellcheck` and `shfmt` run via pre-commit on `scripts/*.sh` (see `.pre-commit-config.yaml`).
436	
437	## Docker Testing
438	
439	```bash
440	# Build and run the bats smoke suite
441	just docker-test
442	
443	# Interactive devbox shell
444	just docker-run
445	
446	# Build specific profiles
447	just docker-desktop    # Ubuntu desktop profile
448	just docker-china      # China mirror profile
449	
450	# CentOS-family (centos_server profile) — covers RHEL-family install paths.
451	# Each base image has two flavors (sudo and noRoot) to match the actual
452	# corporate target (CentOS 7 + noRoot=true) and the modern dnf path.
453	just docker-run-centos7-noroot   # CentOS 7 + noRoot=true (corporate scenario)
454	just docker-run-rocky9           # Rocky Linux 9, sudo path
455	just docker-test-centos7         # bats smoke suite on CentOS 7
456	just docker-test-rocky9          # bats smoke suite on Rocky 9
457	just docker-build-centos-all     # build all four CentOS-family images
458	```

945	**Why this matters**: a developer who runs `just upgrade-all` on a Linux
946	host gets brew + mise + uv + npm + cargo + dotnet + gem + flatpak +

951

954	- The gap is sharpest on **noRoot Linux** where GitHub releases are

1195	
1196	## Decision tree for new tools
1197	
1198	```
1199	Is the tool needed BEFORE ansible runs?
1200	├── Yes → Bootstrap script (run_once_before_*) — only if absolutely necessary
1201	└── No → continue
1202	
1203	Is it a runtime / language interpreter (node, ruby, python, rust, go, dotnet)?
1204	├── Yes → mise (dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl) — except python (use uv)
1205	└── No → continue
1206	
1207	Is it a Python CLI tool?
1208	├── Yes → uv (append to python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml)
1209	│         · For LLM-related, llm_tools/defaults/main.yml
1210	│         · Needs gcc ≥ 9? Set needs_modern_gcc: true
1211	│         · Writes companion binaries? Set both with_executables_from and extra_binaries
1212	└── No → continue
1213	
1214	Is it a Node/JS CLI tool?
1215	├── Yes → npm via mise (append to js_cli_tools/defaults/main.yml)
1216	│         · Agent CLI? Add to coding_agents/tasks/main.yml instead
1217	└── No → continue
1218	
1219	Is it a Rust crate that's well-published on crates.io?
1220	├── Yes → cargo (rust_cargo_tools/defaults/main.yml cargo_tools entry)
1221	│         · Needs build deps or git-source? Hard-code in tasks/main.yml
1222	└── No → continue
1223	
1224	Is it a Ruby gem?
1225	├── Yes → gem (ruby_gem_tools/defaults/main.yml)
1226	│         · Skipped on noRoot Linux automatically
1227	└── No → continue
1228	
1229	Is it a .NET global tool?
1230	├── Yes → dotnet tool (dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml)
1231	└── No → continue
1232	
1233	Is it a Go CLI tool (installable via `go install`)?
1234	├── Yes → go (append to go_tools/defaults/main.yml: name=<module>@<ver>, binary=<cmd>)
1235	│         · Installs to ~/.local/bin via GOBIN; gated on installExtraRuntimes
1236	│         · Upgrade handled by cat_go in scripts/upgrade_tools.sh (just upgrade-go)
1237	└── No → continue
1238	
1239	Is the tool a coding agent CLI (vendor-distributed, ships its own installer)?
1240	├── Yes → curl-installer in coding_agents/tasks/main.yml
1241	│         · Match existing pattern (Claude / OpenCode / Cursor)
1242	│         · Pass --no-modify-path or equivalent (don't mutate shell rc)
1243	│         · Add to cat_agents in scripts/upgrade_tools.sh
1244	│         · Update AICAP SSOT (dot_config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh) +
1245	│           four Python AGENT_CONFIG dicts (see AGENTS.md hard invariant)
1246	└── No → continue
1247	
1248	Is it a Yazi plugin?
1249	├── Yes → ya pkg (Yazi's plugin manager; § 15). Lockfile
1250	│         dot_config/yazi/package.toml (chezmoi-managed), materialized by
1251	│         run_onchange_after_45_yazi_plugins. `ya pkg add owner/repo:plugin`,
1252	│         copy package.toml back; upgrade via `ya pkg upgrade` (just upgrade-yazi-plugins)
1253	└── No → continue
1254	
1255	Is it macOS-shipped, GUI app?
1256	├── Yes → brew cask in Brewfile.darwin.tmpl
1257	│         · Gate on installAiDesktopApps for AI apps
1258	└── No → continue
1259	
1260	Is it macOS-shipped, CLI?
1261	├── Yes → brew formula in the relevant role's tasks/main.yml
1262	│         · Add Linux fallback (apt or GitHub release) in same role
1263	│         · Consider whether macOS-only is OK (e.g. terminal-notifier)
1264	└── No → continue
1265	
1266	Is it Linux-only, distro-packaged?
1267	├── Yes → apt / yum in the relevant role's tasks/main.yml
1268	│         · become: true + tags: [sudo]
1269	│         · Add user-level GitHub-release fallback for noRoot
1270	└── No → continue
1271	
1272	Is it Linux-only, vendor-distributed (ships its own install.sh)?
1273	├── Yes → curl-installer in the relevant role
1274	│         · Use creates: guard
1275	│         · If the binary lands outside ~/.local/bin, add a PATH prepend
1276	│           to dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl
1277	└── No → continue
1278	
1279	GitHub release tarball (most reliable for everything else):
1280	└── Copy the canonical pattern from devtools/tasks/main.yml
1281	    · block: + rescue: (vendor outages happen)
1282	    · retries: 3, delay: 5, timeout: 120 on get_url
1283	    · Compute arch via target_architecture
1284	    · Extract to ~/.local/bin (user) or /usr/local/bin (sudo + tags: [sudo])
1285	    · ⚠️ This binary will NOT be upgraded automatically (see § Coverage gaps)
1286	```
1287

1289	
1290	1. If the tool ships shell completions (`<tool> completion zsh|bash`),
1291	   add a `regen` row in `scripts/generate_completions.sh` (per AGENTS.md
1292	   cross-file rule)

1295	   `docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md` Section F (two hand-written completion
1296	   files + row in section F + row in `docs/shells/aliases.md`)
1297	3. If the tool has a notable upgrade story (self-update subcommand,
1298	   etc.), add a category or extend an existing one in

1300	4. If the tool replaces another tool, add the deprecated path to

```text
---HEAD---
---
# Developer CLI tools role
# Tools: bat, bats, gh, glab, diffnav, gh-dash, gh-notify, eza, git-delta, git-graph, tldr, glow, gum, vhs, freeze, thefuck, zoxide, direnv, yazi, superfile, tmux, sesh, worktrunk, workmux, zellij, herdr, btop, htop, duckdb, rclone, coreutils, taplo, television, pandoc, doxx, libreoffice, tailspin, lnav, grc, ccze (Linux only), dasel, yq, jnv, witr, figlet, toilet, lolcat, fastfetch, mosh, chafa, poppler, sevenzip (7zz), resvg (yazi preview deps)

# =============================================================================
# macOS - all via Homebrew
# =============================================================================

- name: Tap diffnav formula (macOS)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew_tap:
    name: dlvhdr/formulae
    state: present

- name: Tap raine/workmux formula (macOS)
  # workmux is a tmux + git-worktree orchestrator with first-class agent
  # status icons (🤖 working / 💬 waiting / ✅ done) rendered into the tmux
  # window list. Coexists with worktrunk (`wt`); see docs/tools/workmux.md
  # for the wt-vs-wm split.
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew_tap:
    name: raine/workmux
    state: present

# Homebrew 6.0 added a formula-trust security gate: `brew install` refuses to
# load formulae from third-party taps until the tap is explicitly trusted
# ("Error: Refusing to load formula <tap>/<formula> from untrusted tap"). The
# homebrew_tap module has no trust parameter, so trust via `brew trust`.
# Idempotent + back-compatible: older Homebrew has no trust concept, so
# `tap-info` won't contain "Untrusted" and the trust task no-ops (no version
# gate needed). Keep this loop in sync with the third-party taps above — add any
# new third-party tap here too. See pitfalls/homebrew-6-refuses-untrusted-tap-formula.md
- name: Check trust state of third-party taps (macOS, Homebrew >= 6.0 formula-trust gate)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  ansible.builtin.command: "brew tap-info {{ item }}"
  loop:
    - dlvhdr/formulae
    - raine/workmux
  register: devtools_tap_info
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Trust untrusted third-party taps (macOS)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
    - "'Untrusted' in item.stdout"
  ansible.builtin.command: "brew trust {{ item.item }}"
  loop: "{{ devtools_tap_info.results }}"
  loop_control:
    label: "{{ item.item }}"
  changed_when: true

- name: Install developer CLI tools (macOS)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew:
    name:
      - bat
      - bats-core
      - gh
      - glab
```
</details></tool-use>
